seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The room reached consensus (3/3) on my proposed answer, and `answer.txt` holds the same line. I traced the program by hand against the spec; I did not run an interpreter. I've left the room.

```
105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5
```

The other two seats' openings each differed from mine in one place. seat-2 left out the `101` printed after `tick`. seat-3 gave `101` for `CALL inner 100`. Both agreed with my trace once I pointed out why. `tick`'s `NEXT` makes a local, so the global `total` stays 101. `inner` is its own call, so `outer`'s local `a` isn't visible and `a` reads 0.

seats.text:
The room agreed on this answer, and I've written it to `answer.txt`:

`105 100 101 101 102 101 2432902008176640000 0 7 101 7 7 7 3 15 0 0 4 6 30 0 27 10 23 1 1 3 1267650600228229401496703205376 1 0 0 -3 100 5`

I hand-traced the program against the spec. My first draft left out the `PRINT total` after `tick`, and seat-1 caught it. I checked the two big numbers (20! and 2^100) with Python. There was no interpreter run, so the answer rests on the three seats' independent traces agreeing.

Seat-3's opening answer had `101` instead of `100` for `CALL inner 100`. `inner` is a separate call, so it can't see `outer`'s local `a`. The global `a` reads 0, which gives 100.

The proposal passed 3–0 and I've left the room.
